interpretations: Long rental means `rental_duration` >= 5. Benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages over the ratings present among long-rental films.
Long rental means `rental_duration` > 5. Benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages over the ratings present among long-rental films.
Long rental means `rental_duration` >= 5. Benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages computed over all films of every rating, with no duration filter.
Long rental means `rental_duration` > 5. Benchmark is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages computed over all films of every rating, with no duration filter.
The per-rating average is the mean over films of (`rental_rate` / `rental_duration`), computed film by film and then averaged.
The per-rating average is AVG(`rental_rate`) / AVG(`rental_duration`) within each rating group.
The film count is the number of long-rental films in the rating, including any with a missing ratio.
The film count is the number of long-rental films in the rating with a non-missing `rental_rate` / `rental_duration` value.
The benchmark is the simple mean of the per-rating averages, with each rating weighted equally, not the pooled mean over all films.
The final column is the rating's average divided by the benchmark, giving a relative index where 1 equals the benchmark.
If the benchmark is NULL (no ratings with a non-missing average), the query returns zero rows.
Films with a NULL `rating` form their own group and are included in the output.
Films with a NULL `rating` are excluded from both the groups and the benchmark.
The benchmark is included as a column on every output row.
Output is ordered by `rating` or by the ratio. No ordering is specified.
queries:
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS benchmark
FROM (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
  GROUP BY rating
);
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_len) AS bench FROM per_rating
)
SELECT f.rating
FROM film f, benchmark b
WHERE f.rental_duration >= 5
GROUP BY f.rating, b.bench
HAVING AVG(f.length) > b.bench;
SELECT rating
FROM film
WHERE rental_duration > 5
GROUP BY rating
HAVING AVG(length) > (
  SELECT AVG(avg_len)
  FROM (
    SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_len
    FROM film
    GROUP BY rating
  )
);
SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) FROM film GROUP BY rating
SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) FROM film GROUP BY rating;
